answer.location_description: Whole image: a horizontal stripe or grating pattern that repeats every 4 rows (2 bright rows, 2 dark rows) and spans all 24 columns from top to bottom. It is not confined to the nodule.
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units act as phase-matched horizontal-grating detectors. Group A: units 0, 3, 14, 18, 23, 24, 26 and 28, with large positive biases of about 75–99, so they are on by default. Group B: units 5, 11 and 15, with negative biases of about -46 to -75, so they are off unless driven. Each unit's positive and negative rows roughly cancel for uniform brightness, so the units respond to the stripe pattern itself. When stripes of B's phase are present, group A is suppressed and group B switches on. Group A feeds layer-2 units u6, u7, u9 and u12, whose output weights (-55, -73, -56, -69) push toward benign. Group B feeds layer-2 units u1, u4 and u8, which also receive strong negative weights from group A, and these push toward malignant (output weights +85, +99, +59). The net effect is that the presence of the stripe artifact pushes the logit toward malignant, while its absence leaves the default benign pathway active.
answer.evidence: Group A units have positive rows 2–3, 6–7, 10–11, 14–15, 18–19 and 22–23, and negative rows 0–1, 4–5, 8–9, 12–13, 16–17 and 20–21. This holds consistently across all 24 columns, e.g. unit 14 r6 runs up to 86 and r4 down to -51. Group B (units 5, 11, 15) has exactly the opposite phase: rows 0–1, 4–5, 8–9, 12–13, 16–17 and 20–21 are strongly positive (unit 15 r4–r5 values 40–76), and the alternate rows are negative. A full-image, 4-row-period grating is not a nodule or lung property. The remaining 21 first-layer units carry only small, unstructured weights. Layer-2 wiring: u4 takes -60/-90/-49/-90/-77 from units 0/14/18/24/28 and +24/+28/+32 from units 5/11/15, with output weight +99. u8 takes -72/-86/-71/-81 from units 0/3/18/26 and +28/+58/+38 from units 5/11/15, with output weight +59. u6, u7, u9 and u12 take large positive weights (60–99) from group A, with negative output weights.
answer.main_feature: Superimposed on the stripe detectors is a modest central nodule template. Group A is negative around rows 8–9 and 15–16, columns 9–12, and positive around rows 10–11, columns 16–18; group B mirrors this. This reads as a weak sensitivity to nodule brightness, shape and margin in the centre, but most structured weight goes to the stripe pattern.
